## How they got there
Borussia Dortmund reached the final as runners-up after losing to Real Madrid 0-2, having beaten more teams than 66% of their season's peers in long passes and 56% in shots per game. These high-volume attacking metrics helped them navigate a knockout stage involving 16 teams, where they also covered an average distance of 112.3 km per game to outperform just 6% of the league on that specific stat.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned an 8.9% probability of reaching the final, which sits below the 12.5% base rate for a random knockout team and corresponds to a rank of 8 among all participants. With an expected stage score of 0.38, the figure is nearest to the quarter-finals on the scale where 0 represents elimination before that round. Since only the top two ranks qualify as a model selection and Dortmund finished eighth, the system would not have picked them despite their actual performance.

## Weak spots
The team beat fewer opponents than any other stat in shot conversion at just 12% of teams and possession at 20%, marking these as clear areas where they underperformed relative to peers. Additionally, while the model marked down passes per game with a negative contribution of -0.13, Dortmund still ranked better than only 25% of their season's teams on this metric. The low ranking on shot conversion and possession suggests limited efficiency in converting chances and controlling play during the campaign.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat drove, propelled, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
